verdict: Caution: lend selectively to compliant, effluent-ready tanners with verified export orders; avoid job-work units and anyone with a sealed ETP or unpaid wages.
title: Unnao leather tanning: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business is, and where the cash sits
**A tannery buys raw hides and skins, soaks, lims, tans, and finishes them, then sells wet-blue, crust or finished leather to shoe and garment makers.** Cash goes out on hides and chemicals at the front and comes back 60-120 days later from buyers, so the working-capital cycle is the whole business. **The two costs that decide survival are raw hides and effluent treatment, not labour.** Pricing power is thin: buyers quote against Kanpur and Chennai tanners, so a unit without a finishing line sells a commodity. **Capex is the ETP and the drums; a tannery that has not spent on effluent is one inspection away from a stop order.**

## What has changed in Unnao now
**The local file is thin and mostly bad.** A tannery was sealed for discharging contaminated water [3], and a worker was electrocuted at a leather company gate with a compensation protest [1]. Both are 2026 and both point to the same weakness: safety and effluent compliance are the binding constraint, not demand. **Export orders are the second break: foreign buyers reportedly refused about Rs 500 crore of orders in the Kanpur-Unnao belt [2].** That is a local report from March 2026, so treat the number as dated and ask each borrower for its own order book. **The state backdrop is better than the national one: UP GST collections rose 14.2% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], while India-wide exports fell 3.0% Apr-to-date in USD [D].** So the domestic UP market is where the growth is, and exports are where the risk is.

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue tanners selling into the UP domestic shoe and safety-boot chain, and units with a working ETP and a finishing line.** Peer evidence supports this: Super Tannery's Jun-2026 revenue was Rs 76 Cr, up 9.4% YoY, with net profit Rs 3 Cr, up 5.3% [4], and it makes safety boots and work shoes from buffalo hide [6]. **Avoid pure job-work tanners, units with a sealed or unbuilt ETP, and anyone whose order book is one foreign buyer.** When a proposal lands, check the ETP consent order and the last inspection report first; if the consent is expired or conditional, ask for the closure notice history before touching the file.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the fixed assets.** Fund against a stock-and-book-debt statement, keep the limit tied to verified receivables, and take the ETP consent as a covenant. **Take monthly: GST returns, stock statement, debtor ageing, electricity bill, and ETP running log.** Because wet work can close for around 20-30 days under government regulation, requiring 1-2 months of inventory [10], size the limit for a 30-day stoppage, not a normal month. **Peer results show margin is thin even when revenue grows [4][5], so do not stretch tenure to win the account.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the ETP log and the electricity bill together: a falling power bill with a full order book means the drums are idle.** Watch wage payments; the Unnao death and protest [1] show how fast a labour event becomes a closure. Watch forex: peers without a hedging policy booked losses of Rs 0.45 crore in FY24 and Rs 0.57 crore in FY23 [8][9], so ask every exporter for its unhedged position. **If a borrower's export share is rising while India-wide exports fall 3.0% [D], ask which buyer replaced the lost order.**

sales falling while stock rises -> cut limit and ask for debtor ageing
power bill drops with orders on hand -> site visit within a week
unhedged export receivables above policy -> require hedging before renewal
arrears or protest at gate -> stop renewal and reassess
single buyer above half of sales -> ask for the replacement buyer plan
